articles.title: Secret Claude tracker shocks users after Anthropic’s anti-surveillance stance
articles.subtitle: Anthropic accused of spying on users; engineer says “experiment” is over.
articles.author: Ashley Belanger
articles.summary: Anthropic accused of spying on users; engineer says “experiment” is over.
body: Anthropic accused of spying on users; engineer says “experiment” is over.

Anthropic quickly removed a tracker secretly monitoring Claude Code users in China after a security researcher exposed the hidden code and condemned the spyware-like tracking as a “serious breach of user trust.”

Last week, a web developer known as “Thereallo” was researching privacy issues in Claude Code and was shocked to find that the AI firm was using “prompt steganography” to hide code that tracks Chinese users “in plain sight.” This code wasn’t malicious, but it was sending information to Anthropic that most users wouldn’t detect, relying on shorthand markers to quietly flag users’ timezone, proxy, and potential connection to Chinese AI labs that Anthropic has accused of distillation attacks .

On X, Anthropic engineer Thariq Shihipar confirmed that the tracker was added to Claude Code as an “experiment” in March. According to Shihipar, the code “was meant to prevent account abuse from unauthorized resellers and protect against distillation.” Regarding the former, The Washington Post found unauthorized retailers have sold access to free models for $1 a month, and pro subscriptions that can cost $100 monthly sell for “as little as $12.”
Supposedly, Anthropic has “actually been meaning to take this down for a while,” Shihipar said of the hidden code, because engineers have “landed stronger mitigations since then.”

Privacy advocates were not happy with the explanation, though, warning that the code is evidence that Anthropic is willing to cross lines to surveil users. That’s perhaps especially surprising, considering that Anthropic riled the Trump administration by refusing to allow the US government to use Claude to surveil US users. The AI firm has since sued the White House over the clash.
The Post suggested that the tracker incident is a sign that US firms like Anthropic are taking “increasingly aggressive measures” to block Chinese AI firms from copying their models.

A more defensive stance has apparently become critical. In the past year, Chinese firms have “consistently matched” US firms’ model capabilities “within months,” the Post reported. Most recently, “a new, free AI model from Chinese company Zhipu AI was better at finding computer vulnerabilities than Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 model, which was released in May,” the Post reported.

To lock in a 12- or possibly even 24-month lead for the US, Anthropic has said the US must ramp up interventions, using a range of possible penalties to combat distillation attacks , including blocking access to advanced models, chips, and data centers in the US.
Although distillation isn’t illegal (leading US firms do it, too), prompting models like Claude millions of times in order to quickly advance Chinese models violates Anthropic’s user terms.

To end the endless copying, Anthropic has joined OpenAI in urging the US to view distillation attacks as a form of intellectual property theft. At a recent Senate hearing, Sen. Tim Scott (R-S.C.) agreed legal intervention is needed, arguing that the US needs “to carefully craft export control policy that is clear and concise” to stop China from using such attacks to “gain a technological edge,” the Post reported.

It’s clear that Chinese firms are distilling US models, the Post reported. In February, Chinese researchers at Peking University and the state-funded Chinese Academy of Sciences “developed methods to detect signs of distillation in leading large language models” and found that most Chinese models “showed substantial evidence of distillation,” primarily of US models. One of Alibaba’s Qwen AI models—which Anthropic has since claimed was advanced after the largest distillation attack ever on Claude in June—“repeatedly appeared to mimic” Claude in February. In some intensive tests, the model would even sometimes slip up and identify itself as Claude, researchers found.

paragraphTranslations: Anthropic被指控监视用户；工程师表示“实验”已经结束。
在一名安全研究员揭露了隐藏代码并谴责这种类似间谍软件的追踪是“严重违反用户信任”之后，Anthropic迅速移除了一个秘密监控中国Claude Code用户的追踪器。
上周，一位名为“Thereallo”的网络开发人员在研究Claude Code中的隐私问题时，震惊地发现这家人工智能公司使用了“提示隐写术”来隐藏代码，以“明目张胆”的方式追踪中国用户。这段代码并非恶意，但它向Anthropic发送了大多数用户无法察觉的信息，依赖于速记标记来悄悄标记用户的时区、代理以及与中国AI实验室的潜在联系，Anthropic曾指控这些实验室进行蒸馏攻击。
在X日，Anthropic工程师Thariq Shihipar确认，追踪器是在3月份作为“实验”添加到Claude Code中的。据Shihipar称，该代码“旨在防止未经授权的转售者滥用账户，并保护免受蒸馏攻击”。关于前者，《华盛顿邮报》发现未经授权的零售商以每月1美元的价格出售免费模型的访问权限，而每月可能花费100美元的专业订阅则以“低至12美元”的价格出售。
Shihipar表示，Anthropic“实际上一直打算拆除这段隐藏代码”，因为工程师们“自那以后已经实施了更强有力的缓解措施”。
然而，隐私倡导者对这一解释并不满意，警告说这段代码是Anthropic愿意越过界限监视用户的证据。考虑到Anthropic曾因拒绝允许美国政府使用Claude监视美国用户而激怒了特朗普政府，这或许尤其令人惊讶。这家AI公司后来因冲突起诉了白宫。
《邮报》暗示，追踪器事件是一个迹象，表明像Anthropic这样的美国公司正在采取“越来越激进的措施”来阻止中国AI公司复制他们的模型。
显然，采取更防御性的立场已经变得至关重要。在过去的一年里，《邮报》报道，中国公司“始终在几个月内”与美国公司的模型能力相匹配。最近，“中国公司Zhipu AI推出的一款新的免费AI模型在发现计算机漏洞方面比Anthropic在5月发布的Claude Opus 4.8模型更胜一筹”，《邮报》报道。
为了锁定美国可能的12个月甚至24个月的领先优势，Anthropic表示，美国必须加大干预力度，使用一系列可能的惩罚措施来打击蒸馏攻击，包括阻止访问美国的先进模型、芯片和数据中心。
尽管蒸馏本身并不违法（领先的美国公司也在做），但为了迅速推进中国模型而促使像Claude这样的模型数百万次违反了Anthropic的用户条款。
为了结束无休止的复制，Anthropic已经加入了OpenAI，敦促美国将蒸馏攻击视为一种知识产权盗窃行为。在最近的一次参议院听证会上，参议员Tim Scott（R-S.C.）同意需要法律干预，认为美国需要“精心制定清晰简洁的出口控制政策”，以阻止中国利用这种攻击“获得技术优势”，《邮报》报道。

《邮报》报道，很明显中国公司正在蒸馏美国模型。今年2月，来自北京大学和国家资助的中国科学院的中国研究人员“开发了检测领先大型语言模型中蒸馏迹象的方法”，并发现大多数中国模型“显示出明显的蒸馏证据”，主要是美国的模型。阿里巴巴的一款Qwen AI模型——Anthropic后来声称，这款模型在6月对Claude进行了有史以来最大的蒸馏攻击后得到了提升——“反复出现模仿”Claude的情况。研究人员发现，在一些密集测试中，该模型甚至有时会出错，并将自己识别为Claude。

articles.title: What is the oldest American object ever launched into space?
articles.subtitle: From a Revolutionary War flag to the Statue of Liberty...
articles.author: Robert Pearlman
articles.summary: From a Revolutionary War flag to the Statue of Liberty...
body: Did you know that the space shuttle once launched the Statue of Liberty into space?

In fact, there were two “Lady Liberties” on board Discovery when it lifted off on its fourth flight in April 1985. To be fair, each statue was only 15 inches tall (38.1 centimeters), but they were also each made of copper that was removed from the full-size statue during its then-still-ongoing restoration.

After the weeklong STS-51D mission was over, one of the space-flown statues was placed on display, and the other was melted down to create copper seals, which were then sold to the public by the Statue of Liberty Ellis Island Centennial Commission.
The copper dated back to the statue’s original 1875 to 1884 construction. A gift from France, the Statue of Liberty was originally intended to commemorate the United States’ centennial in 1876.

Now, as the US enters its next 250 years , there have been an additional four decades of spaceflights when other objects from American history have been carried into Earth orbit. Which raises the question: What is the oldest known piece of Americana to have been launched off the planet?

For the purposes of this article, Americana refers to any piece of memorabilia that dates as far back as the Revolutionary War and the signing of the Declaration of Independence in 1776. There are certainly older objects that have entered space—a 1611 Jamestown “luggage tag” from the first permanent English settlement was flown on Atlantis in 2007, for example—but fall outside this article’s scope.

John Glenn, one of the original Mercury astronauts and a US senator, was the oldest person to fly into space when he launched on a 1998 Discovery mission at the age of 77. Among the items he chose to take with him were two connected to early American history.

“After consultation with staff in the Office of Senate Curator, the Senate Historical Office and Senate Library, Senator Glenn selected this ‘Manual of Parliamentary Practice’ for the STS-95 OFK,” the Senate Curator’s Office described in a 2023 article , referring to the Official Flight Kit that held mementos and memorabilia for post-flight presentation. “The ‘Manual of Parliamentary Practice’ was a practical choice because of its relatively small size and weight, but it is also a meaningful text in Senate history.”

Written by Thomas Jefferson in 1801 while he was serving as vice president (and therefore the head of the Senate), the manual influenced both houses of Congress as to how to approach order and decorum.

Glenn also took with him a 13-star flag that was used to identify General George Washington on the battlefield. Believed to be inspired by the details on the general’s uniform in 1777, Washington’s Headquarters Flag (also known as the Commander-in-Chief standard) flew with Glenn in the lead-up to the bicentennial commemorations of Washington’s death in 1799.

Both the flag and the manual, though, were reproductions. The originals are in museums and deemed too fragile and irreplaceable to risk being launched into space. The copy that Glenn flew was a 1993 reprint, and the flag was made for Glenn to fly in 1998.

Another replica flag steeped in American history was aboard the International Space Station from November 2014 through June 2015. NASA astronaut Terry Virts was provided the 15-star flag by Fort McHenry in Maryland, after it was flown over the historic site for Flag Day during the bicentennial year of the Battle of Baltimore. The original of that flag was seen by Francis Scott Key to “yet wave,” leading him to write a poem that became the US anthem, The Star-Spangled Banner , in 1814.

paragraphTranslations: 你知道吗，航天飞机曾经把自由女神像送入太空？
实际上，在1985年4月发现号第四次飞行时，有两座“自由女神”在船上。公平地说，每个雕像只有15英寸高（38.1厘米），但它们也都是由在全尺寸雕像正在进行的修复过程中移除的铜制成的。
为期一周的STS-51D任务结束后，一座太空飞行的雕像被展出，另一座被熔化制成铜印，然后由自由女神像埃利斯岛百年委员会向公众出售。
这些铜可以追溯到雕像最初的1875年至1884年的建造时期。自由女神像是法国的礼物，最初是为了纪念美国建国一百周年在1876年。
现在，随着美国进入其接下来的250年，还有另外四十年的太空飞行，其他美国历史上的物体被带入地球轨道。这引出了一个问题：已知最古老的美国文物是什么时候被发射到这个星球之外的？
为了本文的目的，美国文物指的是任何可以追溯到独立战争和1776年独立宣言签署的纪念品。当然，有更古老的物体进入了太空——例如，2007年亚特兰蒂斯号上飞行的一个1611年詹姆斯敦“行李标签”来自第一个永久性的英国定居点，但这超出了本文的范围。
约翰·格伦，水星计划的原始宇航员之一和美国参议员，当他在1998年发现号任务中以77岁高龄进入太空时，是进入太空的最年长的人。他选择带走的物品中，有两件与美国早期历史有关。
“在与参议院馆长办公室、参议院历史办公室和参议院图书馆的工作人员协商后，格伦参议员为STS-95 OFK选择了这本‘议会实践手册’，”参议院馆长办公室在2023年的一篇文章中描述，指的是官方飞行包，其中包含了飞行后赠送的纪念品和纪念品。“‘议会实践手册’是一个实用的选择，因为它相对较小的尺寸和重量，但它也是参议院历史上一个有意义的文本。”
手册由托马斯·杰斐逊在1801年撰写，当时他担任副总统（因此是参议院的负责人），手册影响了国会两院如何处理秩序和礼仪的方式。
格伦还带了一面13星旗，这面旗子被用来在战场上识别乔治·华盛顿将军。这面旗子被认为是受到1775年将军制服上细节的启发，华盛顿总部旗（也被称为总司令标准）随着格伦在1799年华盛顿逝世二百周年纪念活动前飞入太空。
不过，这面旗子和手册都是复制品。原作在博物馆里，被认为太脆弱且不可替代，不能冒险被送入太空。格伦飞行的副本是1993年的重印版，而旗帜是为格伦在1998年飞行制作的。
另一面充满美国历史的复制旗帜在2014年11月至2015年6月期间在国际空间站上。美国宇航局宇航员特里·维尔茨由马里兰州的麦克亨利堡提供了15星旗，在巴尔的摩战役二百周年年的国旗日期间，这面旗帜在历史遗址上空飞行。那面旗帜的原作被弗朗西斯·斯科特·基看到“仍在飘扬”，导致他在1814年写了一首诗，这首诗成为了美国国歌《星条旗》。

The flag, a reproduction, was inspired by the one used to identify General George Washington on the battlefield in 1777. Glenn also took a 'Manual of Parliamentary Practice' written by Thomas Jefferson in 1801. Both items are reproductions; the originals are in museums.

Another replica flag with American history is the 15-star flag aboard the International Space Station from November 2014 to June 2015. It was provided by Fort McHenry in Maryland and is connected to the US anthem, The Star-Spangled Banner.
